label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all fall in the higher range compared to other profiles, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring psychological distress alongside heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness as indicated by a UCLA-8 mean of approximately 1.78
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology with a PHQ-9 mean of approximately 1.81
Notably high anxiety symptoms with a GAD-7 mean of approximately 2.27, the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties alongside intensive digital media engagement
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of psychological distress and heavy social-media involvement observed in this group

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social media use is relatively light, averaging roughly 2.8 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour bracket). With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 0.78, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 0.27, and a GAD-7 anxiety mean of 0.03, this group consistently scores well below clinical concern thresholds across all three psychological well-being measures. The profile is based on 108 respondents in the training sample.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, typically 1–3 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social media usage averaging approximately 2.8 hours
Very low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ~0.78 on normalized scale)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ~0.27 on normalized scale)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ~0.03 on normalized scale)
Pattern of psychological well-being consistently below clinical thresholds across all measured domains
tone: Stable, psychologically resilient, and socially balanced

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness yet comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms, while spending nearly five hours per day on social media. Their loneliness scores sit above the sample norm, suggesting persistent feelings of social disconnection, but these do not translate into proportionally high clinical mood or anxiety symptoms. Their heavy daily social-media engagement may serve as a compensatory social outlet or may itself contribute to their sense of isolation.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) relative to other profiles
Below-average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Below-average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Heavy daily social-media use averaging close to 5 hours
Possible reliance on social media as a primary channel for social connection
tone: Socially disconnected yet emotionally stable; quietly seeking connection through digital engagement

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a group of 217 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, paired with relatively light daily social-media use averaging roughly 1.6 hours. Their psychological well-being scores are consistently below scale midpoints, suggesting a generally healthy mental-health profile. These individuals hold graduate-level or higher education and report 1–3 hours of daily social-media engagement.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.22, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82)
Low anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.90)
Social-media engagement within a moderate 1–3 hour daily window
tone: Stable, psychologically resilient, and measured in digital engagement
